label: yes
controls_available: Wind the clock starts the outcome phase; Submit Expedition is administrative.
Full interaction accepts ArrowUp/ArrowRight/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft or W/A/S/D for UP/RIGHT/DOWN/LEFT, and Space for WAIT; repeated key events are ignored.

One outcome-affecting keyboard action is available during the first 1150 ms gold window of each 1800 ms beat. Off-beat keyboard presses are recorded as no-ops, and only one action can be used in a beat.
The visible task controls include the grid, player, exit, sentries, health, beat pulse, beat label, roster phase text, and lancer danger tiles.
autonomous_processes: After the clock starts, elapsed task time and the visible pulse advance continuously; the gold action window closes at 1150 ms of each 1800 ms beat.

At every 1800 ms beat boundary, live sentries act without a new agent action. Crawlers and active hoppers chase one tile when their phase permits; an active lancer damages an adjacent player while remaining rooted. The beat increments and the action-used flag resets.
After 100 beats the clock is exhausted; submission remains administrative.

grouped_control_modes.name: full_keyboard_beat_action
grouped_control_modes.scope: Every outcome-affecting keyboard opportunity across generated seeds, beats, and attempts in the full interaction configuration; start, submit, and off-beat no-ops are excluded.

clause_i.reason: No policy using only prior keys and task times can be optimal for every history in this grouped mode: the generator independently randomizes walls, start, exit, enemy positions, and enemy phase offsets, so the same action history and time can present different boards and different best next directions or waits after one beat. The current visible board and sentry state are necessary.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded 300 ms window with the configured three chronological frames is sufficient. The current frame exposes the player, walls, exit, enemy positions and health, while the roster, shield styling, danger tiles, beat label, and pulse expose sentry phase and the action window. The sentry transition is deterministic from that visible state, so a policy can use the recent frame window to predict the next beat and select the delayed-optimal keyboard action.

clause_iii.reason: Use D=full keyboard beat actions, Delta=1800 ms, and take t just after a beat boundary with a vulnerable hopper adjacent to the player. A concrete source-only replay of generated seed 1 reaches beat 13 with player [2,3], hopper [3,3], hopper hp 2 and offset 1 (phase 0): RIGHT immediately returns hit. With no action, the next boundary occurs about 1750 ms later, success remains possible, and the hopper is phase 1 at H_t^tau; the same RIGHT returns shield, whereas WAIT is also a no-op, so RIGHT loses its action advantage. The immediate attack leaves a shorter route, while the delayed action leaves the hopper undamaged and can expose the player to its chase. The loss is caused by hopper phase evolution, not by deadline passage.

common_visible_process: The common process is the visible per-beat sentry phase transition and resulting movement or attack: the roster and board show the phase/position before and after a beat, and that same evolution both makes the best delayed key depend on the screenshot and makes a currently useful attack or evasive move lose value while the agent waits.

pre_run.reason: No successful pre-run solution is available. Before the clock starts, keyboard input is ignored. After it starts, with no outcome-affecting actions the player remains at the generated start, enemy hp never decreases, and the exit is sampled from a cell at Manhattan distance at least 3 from start. Sentries can only damage the stationary player, so no generated instance can clear the sentries and reach the exit without actions.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 is the 8x8, six-wall, crawler/hopper/lancer, two-hp-enemy, three-health profile; full mode is keyboard arrows/WASD/Space; the observation window is 300 ms with three frames and the beat runtime is defined by the mechanic.
The runtime exposes a frame-window observation and 300 ms/three-frame runner options, with keyboard and mouse action surfaces.

The exact profile is used to generate connected seeded boards; start, exit, walls, enemy positions, enemy hp, and phase offsets are generated, with beat_ms 1800, open_ms 1150, and max_beats 100. The generator validates reachability through the replay planner.
The browser initializes visible combat state, accepts directional/WAIT actions, and advances sentries autonomously at beat boundaries according to crawler, hopper, and lancer phases.

The visible render shows beat timing, roster phase text, enemy/player/exit/danger geometry, and full-mode keyboard mapping; only the gold portion calls the action logic, and the input is limited to one used action per beat.
The board, player, enemy types, hopper shield, exit, and lancer danger tiles have distinct visible styling.
The independent replay confirms action effects, phase-dependent hopper shielding, autonomous sentry movement/attacks, and beat reset semantics.
The grader replays every timestamped keyboard event against the beat/open windows and requires the final replayed state to be a live escape.
The source planner treats each action as followed by autonomous advancement and finds routes only through valid beat actions, supporting that action timing and evolving sentry state affect the route.
Verification loads the shared result helper and independent clockbeat replay grader rather than trusting client outcomes.
The ordinary solver starts the clock, waits for each beat, checks the gold-window timing, and sends one keyboard action per route step; it is wiring evidence, not private-state policy evidence.
The verifier helper only loads the exported result through the environment copy function; it does not alter the clockbeat outcome replay.
